name: The Sir Duncan Rice Library
additional_access_notes: A Student ID card is required to enter the upper floor of the building.
location_description: Opened in 2012 and named in honour of former Principal Sir Duncan Rice, the University's main library is a striking seven-storey cube clad in white and clear glass, designed by Schmidt Hammer Lassen and visible across the campus and city. It holds the modern collections plus a quarter of a million historic books and manuscripts, with study spaces, a ground-floor cafe and a public exhibition gallery.

name: King's College
location_description: The historic heart of the University, King's College dates from around 1500 and is crowned by its distinctive Crown Tower. The quadrangle and surrounding buildings remain central to University life and ceremony.

name: New King's
location_description: New King's sits on King's Lawn beside King's College Chapel and Elphinstone Hall, providing lecture and teaching space at the historic core of the Old Aberdeen campus.

name: King's College Chapel
opening_hours_note: Open to visitors on weekdays; services held during term
location_description: King's College Chapel, beneath the iconic Crown Tower, is one of the University's most historic and beautiful spaces. Dating from the early 16th century, the chapel sanctuary contains rare 16th- and 17th-century canvas and timber decoration. It is open to visitors on weekdays and holds regular services during term.

name: King's Conference Centre
opening_hours_note: Open for booked events only — no fixed public hours
location_description: Housed in the former University Library of 1870, King's Conference Centre was converted to its current use in 1991. Its largest venue, King's Auditorium, features stained-glass windows, a barrel-vaulted ceiling and a balcony, and meeting and syndicate rooms are available on the first floor.

name: Elphinstone Hall
opening_hours_note: Open for booked events only — no fixed public hours
location_description: Located by King's Lawn opposite the High Street, Elphinstone Hall was designed and built in 1930 by A. Marshall Mackenzie. One of the University's most recognisable buildings, it serves as a large examination hall and hosts graduation ceremonies, and can also be hired for dining and functions.

name: Taylor Building
location_description: The Taylor Building consists of four large blocks linked by an overhead walkway, spanning the site between the High Street and the Regent Building. It houses the University's language departments, the Law faculty, the Taylor Library, an IT training room and a number of classrooms. It opened in 1964 and commemorates Sir Thomas Murray Taylor, Professor of Law and Principal.

name: Taylor Library
location_description: The Taylor Library is located within the Taylor Building on the King's College campus. Alongside all fields of legal practice and jurisprudence, it houses the Official Publications Collections.

name: Students' Union Building
location_description: An Â£8m dining, leisure and social facility south of St Machar Drive, the Students' Union Building houses a food court catering for up to 450 people, a shop and a cafe. It is home to the Aberdeen University Students' Association (AUSA), which runs over 120 societies, as well as the Careers and Employability Service and Student Advice & Support.

name: Students' Infohub
location_description: The Students' Infohub on the Old Aberdeen campus is the central point for student enquiries and support services.

name: MacRobert Building
additional_access_notes: ID access needed for some computer rooms.
location_description: Opened in 1967 and originally the Agriculture Building, the MacRobert Building was renamed to honour the MacRobert Trust following a Â£9m refurbishment. It houses the School of Education, the Elphinstone Institute, the Department of Music and the Business School, with its main entrance on the King Street side.

name: Meston Building
location_description: One of the largest buildings on campus, the Meston Building stands near the Sir Duncan Rice Library with entrances on the Library plaza and on Meston Walk. With its large lecture theatres it is frequently used by science students. Opened in 1952 as the Chemistry Building by Nobel laureate Sir Robert Robinson, it was later renamed in memory of Baron Meston, Chancellor of the University 1928-1944.

name: Fraser Noble Building
location_description: The Fraser Noble Building sits on the Library plaza opposite the Meston Building and houses the School of Engineering and the Department of Mathematics. Built in 1963 for Natural Philosophy and opened by Nobel laureate Sir G. P. Thomson, it was refurbished and renamed in 1988 after Sir Fraser Noble, Principal 1976-1981.

name: Cruickshank Building
location_description: The Cruickshank Building houses staff from the School of Biological Sciences and is located off St Machar Drive within the Cruickshank Botanic Garden. The refurbished building contains molecular biology, microbiology and environmental physiology laboratories, with controlled-environment growth chambers and glasshouses nearby.

name: Zoology Building
location_description: Opened in 1970, the Zoology Building stands over St Machar Drive next to the Cruickshank Botanic Garden and opposite the Science Teaching Hub, with its main entrance on Tillydrone Avenue. Built in a Brutalist style echoing Marischal College, it houses the School of Biological Sciences and the University's Zoology Museum.

name: Edward Wright Building
location_description: The Edward Wright Building opened in 1975 and houses Social Science departments and the University's IT Services, including five computer rooms for student use. The building has multiple blocks and entrances, the main computer-room entrance being up the small hill behind the Taylor Building bridge. It is named after Edward Maitland Wright, Professor of Mathematics and Principal 1962-1976.

name: St. Mary's Building
location_description: Originally a church on the High Street, the St Mary's Building was extended in 1969 and again in 1980, with its main entrance now on Elphinstone Road near the Students' Union. It contains the Archaeology, Geography and Land Economy departments, along with lecture theatres, several student computer rooms, and the Arkleton Centre for Rural Development Research.

name: Regent Building
location_description: The Regent Building stands on Regent Walk between the University Office and the Taylor Building. Originally built for the Language Centre and the University Television Service, its former TV studio is now the Regent Lecture Theatre, and it also houses the Online Education team.

name: Crombie Annexe
location_description: The Crombie Annexe is the home of the History Department. A three-storey building next to Crombie Hall, it is located to the south of the Meston Building off Meston Walk.

name: William Guild Building
location_description: Built in 1969-70, the William Guild Building contains the Psychology department, and its main entrance also provides access to the Arts Lecture Theatre and features a seating area for relaxation. It commemorates William Guild, Principal of King's College 1639-1651.

name: Science Teaching Hub
location_description: Opened in 2022 and built at a cost of around Â£35m, the Science Teaching Hub stands on the Old Aberdeen campus next to the Sir Duncan Rice Library and the Fraser Noble Building. Designed by Reiach and Hall Architects, it contains modern teaching laboratories for students across the sciences.

name: Multi-Faith Chaplaincy
location_description: The Multi-Faith Chaplaincy on the High Street, opposite New King's, is at heart a place of pastoral care, providing welcome, support and advice to students and staff of all faiths and none. It offers a social Wellbeing Lounge, quiet space, a Muslim prayer room and quiet study space, and hosts society meetings, seminars and inter-faith events.

name: Old Aberdeen Town House
opening_hours_note: Open for booked events only — no fixed public hours
location_description: Old Aberdeen Town House sits at the top of the High Street at the heart of historic Old Aberdeen. A landmark civic building, it provides meeting and function space for the University and community.

name: Cruickshank Botanic Garden
location_description: Established in 1898 on land gifted by Anne Cruickshank, the Cruickshank Botanic Garden is an 11-acre garden off St Machar Drive. Owned jointly by the University and the Cruickshank Botanic Garden Trust, it is open to the public and used extensively for teaching and research by the School of Biological Sciences.

name: Lady MacRobert Memorial Garden
location_description: As part of a memorial garden to Lady MacRobert, the granite wall has the names of her three sons that fell in service during the Second World War, along with a a mosaic that presents the family coat of arms 'Not For Themselves But For Their Native Land'. Alasdair had died in a Civil air accident in 1938.

name: Butchart Recreational Center
location_description: The Butchart Recreation Centre is a key sports and fitness facility operated by the University of Aberdeen on University Road, just south of King's College. Originally constructed in the 1950s, it serves as an important hub for student athletics and the Aberdeen University Students' Association.

name: King's Lawn
location_description: This expansive lawn, outside Elphinstone Hall, offers a great spot to admire the Old Aberdeen’s fantastic architecture.

name: Counceling Service
location_description: The Counceling Service located at 5 Dunbar Street is part of Student Support Services and is open to all students of the University.

name: Aberdeen Sports Village
location_description: Aberdeen Sports Village is the premier sports facility in the North East of Scotland. It is open to students, staff and the public with facilities for athletics, football, swimming, hockey, squash, martial arts and boxing.

name: Edward Wright Annexe
location_description: The Edward Wright Annexe is an addition to the main Edward Wright building. It houses the parts of the Business School and the School of Social Science. The entrance is through the main building and through the door to the North

name: Rocking Horse Nursery
location_description: The Rocking Horse Nursery is situated within the grounds of Crombie Johnston Hall of Residence behind King's Hall. Student and staff parents may use the Nursery.It has facilities for 78 children from 0-5 years of age and moved to custom-built premises in 2015. The building is the first early years setting in Scotland to be built using the Passivhaus (Passive House) design.

name: Backwells Booksellers
location_description: Blackwell's Aberdeen is a charming, academic-focused bookstore located on High Street in the historic heart of Old Aberdeen. Situated within a 15th-century university quarter, it caters primarily to scholars and students, offering a specialized, relaxed environment for browsing.

name: J.G Ross
location_description: A traditional baker and fresh food takeaway outlet, proudly serving the North East of Scotland for over 60 years.

name: Kilau
location_description: Kilau Coffee is a beloved, long-running independent café and community hub located in the heart of historic Old Aberdeen. Situated right on the University of Aberdeen campus next to the iconic King's College, it serves as a highly popular haunt for students, faculty, and local residents alike.

name: Shelter cofe
location_description: Shelter Coffee is a cosy, Scandinavian-style café situated in the historic heart of Old Aberdeen on the University of Aberdeen campus. It is highly regarded for its charming attic seating area, student-friendly prices, and picturesque views of the Mercat Cross and Old Town House.
